content.text: can you make a desktop app for twyne with gpui
I’ll check Twyne’s structure and how a GPUI desktop app could connect to its editor and account data, then build a runnable starting point.

Twyne already has an Electrobun desktop entry point. I’ll add a separate Rust/GPUI app and use the Impeccable skill to carry its existing typography and writing-room layout into the native UI. There’s substantial work already in the tree, so I’ll keep the new app isolated.

*** Add File: /home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/desktop/gpui/README.md
+# Twyne GPUI
+
+A native offline writing room built in Rust with [GPUI Kit 0.7](https://gpui-kit.com/).
+The manuscript, library, notebook, and controls render through GPUI. No browser,
+web server, Bun runtime, or account is needed to run the compiled app.
+
+## Run
+
+Install Rust 1.92 or newer, a C/C++ toolchain, and the system dependencies in
+[GPUI Kit's installation guide](https://gpui-kit.com/docs/installation/).
+The checked-in lockfile pins the Rust dependencies.
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```bash
+bun run desktop.gpui
+```
+
+Or use Cargo directly:
+
+```bash
+cargo run --locked --manifest-path desktop/gpui/Cargo.toml
+```
+
+On Ubuntu/Debian, install the native build libraries:
+
+```bash
+sudo apt-get install build-essential clang pkg-config libfontconfig1-dev \
+  libfreetype6-dev libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev libxcb1-dev \
+  libwayland-dev libssl-dev
+```
+
+Linux needs an X11 or Wayland session and a graphics driver supported by WGPU.
+Native file pickers use the desktop's XDG portal. macOS needs the Xcode command
+line tools; Windows needs the MSVC C++ build tools. The fonts used by Twyne are
+embedded from `src/assets/typst`; their notices are in
+[`public/licenses/typst-fonts.txt`](../../public/licenses/typst-fonts.txt).
+
+To use an isolated library or import files on startup:
+
+```bash
+cargo run --locked --manifest-path desktop/gpui/Cargo.toml -- \
+  --data-dir /tmp/twyne-native-library /path/to/draft.md
+```
+
+Imports create library copies. The original files stay independent.
+
+## Writing room
+
+- **Library:** create and switch manuscripts, search titles, duplicate drafts,
+  and archive/restore them. Archived drafts remain readable and exportable.
+- **Write:** native multiline text editing with selection, clipboard, undo/redo,
+  Unicode, and Markdown source. The title is a separate editable field.
+- **Read:** formatted Markdown using GPUI Kit's native text renderer.
+- **Notebook:** a brief, sources, and loose thoughts saved with each manuscript.
+- **Focus:** hide both side panels while keeping the manuscript and save status.
+- **Find:** case-sensitive literal search with next-match selection and wraparound.
+- **Save:** autosave 700 ms after typing settles. Save, switching manuscripts,
+  opening Read, and closing the window flush current edits immediately.
+
+Whole-document serialization, statistics, and autosave writes run on a background
+executor after typing settles. The keystroke handler marks a revision and restarts
+the debounce timer. Read is refreshed at an explicit boundary.
+
+At narrow widths, the notebook yields to the manuscript. Hide Library to give it
+space, then use Notebook to show it. The minimum window size is 760 × 520.
+
+## Files and storage
+
+**Import** accepts UTF-8 `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, and native `.twyne` files.
+**Export** saves manuscript text to `.md` or `.txt`; change the extension in the
+save dialog to choose. **Export with notebook** saves a portable `.twyne` file
+containing title, body, and notes. Native imports always receive a new document ID.
+
+The `.twyne` format identifies itself as `twyne-gpui`, version 1. It is a desktop
+document format. Web rich-text/Typst documents are not imported as native files;
+use Markdown or text to move writing between the two apps.
+
+The application data location follows each OS's conventions:
+
+| Platform | Default library |
+| --- | --- |
+| Linux | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/twyne-gpui`, or `~/.local/share/twyne-gpui` |
+| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/love.twyne.twyne-gpui` |
+| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\twyne\twyne-gpui\data` |
+
+`TWYNE_GPUI_DATA_DIR` or `--data-dir` overrides this location. **Open library
+folder** reveals the actual path. Each manuscript lives in `manuscripts/<id>.json`.
+
+Writes use a same-directory temporary file, sync it, and atomically replace the
+primary. The previous valid save is kept in `.json.bak`. A damaged primary is
+recovered from that backup when possible and preserved when repaired. Unreadable
+files are left in place, and the app reports them. Older background revisions
+cannot overwrite newer saves. An OS file lock prevents two instances from writing
+one library at the same time.
+
+Save failures keep the text in the current window, display an error, and block
+switching or closing. Retry Save after fixing the problem, or export a copy.
+The editing limit is 5 MB per manuscript, including notebook and title. Autosave
+protects completed saves; a crash or forced termination during the debounce
+interval can lose the most recent unsaved edits.
+
+The library is separate from the web app's IndexedDB and Convex data. This version
+makes no network requests and does not provide account sync, AI editors, voice,
+publishing, rich-text editing, or Typst proof/PDF. Those remain available in the
+web/Electrobun app.
+
+## Keyboard
+
+Use Cmd on macOS and Ctrl on Linux/Windows.
+
+| Shortcut | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + N | New manuscript |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + O | Import manuscript |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + S | Save current edits |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + E | Export text |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + F | Find in manuscript |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + G | Find next occurrence |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + F | Enter/leave focus |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + B | Show/hide library |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + M | Show/hide notebook |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + 1 / 2 | Write / Read |
+| Cmd/Ctrl + Q | Save and quit |
+
+Standard text selection, cut/copy/paste, undo/redo, and Tab navigation are supplied
+by GPUI Kit. File dialogs use your operating system's controls.
+
+## Build and verify
+
+```bash
+bun run desktop.gpui.check
+bun run desktop.gpui.test
+bun run desktop.gpui.test-ui
+bun run desktop.gpui.build
+```
+
+The release executable is `desktop/gpui/target/release/twyne-desktop`
+(`twyne-desktop.exe` on Windows). It can run independently of the repository.
+
+The core tests exercise persistence, Unicode exchange, file-size limits,
+recovery, locking, archive retention, and stale-save protection. The UI tests
+drive real controls to verify writing/notebook saves, immediate draft switching,
+keyboard focus mode, archive/restore, and recovery from a failed save.
+
+The GPUI workflow builds binaries on Linux, macOS, and Windows. These are unsigned
+executables; application bundles, installers, signing, and automatic updates are
+not configured yet. Native runtime and assistive-technology checks remain
+platform-specific.

+
+Twyne's native desktop port uses Rust and [GPUI Kit 0.7](https://gpui-kit.com/).

+the host supplies no inferred persona-mark anchors or provider capabilities.

+capture, folio/quit draft retention, a failed file write followed by the visible
+desk retry action, rejected late acknowledgements, and a route boundary joining
+the exact background save. Core store and standalone view tests cover their
+separate contracts in [the Cast fixture](../cast/CONTRACT.md).
+
+`check-native.py` allocates an isolated Xvfb display and sends mouse/key input
+from a separate XTEST process. It explicitly activates the observed owned
+Twyne window before typing; a focused textarea handle alone does not activate
+a client on an X server without a window manager. Rendered observations supply
+control bounds, actual platform activation and focus. AccessKit omits the
+disabled property for enabled controls; the driver also exercises actual
+New/Cancel activation rather than assuming that absence proves behavior.
+
+The driver follows Board → Manager → Board → Full Analysis → Board, captures
+an unblurred final keystroke before navigation, obstructs the real metadata
+backup write, checks exact accepted disk bytes during failure, then drives
+retry, File only and Ctrl-Q. It checks writer reply count, retained note and
+foreign data, and the unchanged canonical manuscript. Screenshots, geometry,
+logs and saved test records are written to the requested output directory.

content.text:
So far, it’s **one Rust crate using GPUI Kit**, organized into feature modules, plus a Bun helper that reuses Twyne’s document converters.

| Area | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `app/` | Active manuscript, navigation, saving, and feature coordination |
| `editor/` | Document model, commands, history, input, and rendering |
| `insert_menu/`, `gen_ui/`, other features | Their own rules and UI; they emit actions to the manuscript owner |
| Workspace/Source/Proof modules | Canonical Typst, recoverable drafts, conversion, and compilation |
| Native account/AI/audio modules | Separate integration contracts and transport |
| Theme/assets/chrome | Original fonts, colors, artwork, and shared controls |

I’ve documented the boundaries and original-source counterparts in [ARCHITECTURE.md](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/desktop/gpui/ARCHITECTURE.md).

**The structure still needs work.** `app.rs` remains 4,380 lines, and the main editor view is 3,747. The next useful extractions are Source/Proof coordination, library/file actions, and chrome rendering.

My grasp is strongest around offline editing: document ownership, saving, Unicode positions, undo, title layout, and slash commands. Connected sync and AI have prepared foundations, but native end-to-end behavior remains unfinished. Visual parity also needs continued comparison.

The most useful ways to investigate faster are:

- Map each feature to its original implementation and focused checks.
- Reproduce bugs with a small manuscript, explicit selection, view, window size, and scale.
- Test document rules separately from focus/events and actual rendered pixels.
- Give smaller agents bounded reference or fixture tasks, then validate their conclusions.
- Keep exact build receipts so older previews cannot masquerade as current evidence.

That workflow is producing concrete results: **118 mounted desktop tests and strict Clippy pass**, while fresh captures expose remaining table sizing and font-weight differences. Your open preview remains on the prior build; these checks used isolated copies.

Account sync and AI have substantial contracts, but several routes still need real mounted workflows verified.

The biggest improvements would be smaller host modules and one reliable way to trace a feature from its original implementation to its native code, tests, and captures. The module map already provides that path; I’m extending it as new surfaces land.
